prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks with a Chance to Beat the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that will beat the S&P 500 over one year, and I can't either. Over 15-year periods, roughly 9 in 10 professional large-cap fund managers trail the index (per S&P's SPIVA reports). A 10-stock portfolio can beat the market, but it can also trail it badly.

My information also only runs through about May 2026, so I don't know current prices, valuations or recent news. Check each name before buying.

## The list

| # | Stock | Why it could beat the index | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Its Azure cloud business and AI tools sold into its huge business customer base | Heavy AI spending may not pay off quickly |
| 2 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search, YouTube and Google Cloud, plus Waymo (self-driving cars); often cheaper than other tech giants relative to earnings | Antitrust rulings; AI chatbots taking search traffic |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS cloud, a fast-growing ad business and rising retail profits | Consumer slowdown; heavy spending |
| 4 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Manufactures nearly all advanced AI chips for other companies | China–Taiwan tensions |
| 5 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips and data-center networking for big tech companies | High valuation; relies on a few large customers |
| 6 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and power-grid equipment as data centers drive electricity demand | The stock has already risen a lot, so high expectations are priced in |
| 7 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leads in obesity and diabetes drugs (GLP-1s), with new pill versions coming | Drug-price pressure, competition, high valuation |
| 8 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large U.S. bank with a strong balance sheet | Recession and loan losses |
| 9 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a small fee on a huge volume of card payments, with high profit margins | Regulation of card fees; new payment methods such as stablecoins |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Diversified, holds a large cash pile, and tends to hold up in downturns | Likely to lag in strong bull markets; new CEO after Buffett |

The list mixes AI and tech growth (1–6) with healthcare, financials and a defensive holding (7–10). If tech sells off, the last four should soften the blow.

Many of these names are already large parts of the S&P 500. To beat the index, you have to hold something different from it. Owning 10 stocks at 10% each is a concentrated bet on these specific companies, so your results will differ from the index noticeably, in either direction.

## Ways to improve your odds
- **Core and satellite:** Put most of your money (say 70–80%) in an S&P 500 index fund and the rest in picks like these. You get some chance of beating the market without risking large underperformance.
- **Equal-weight and rebalance** once or twice a year so no single stock dominates.
- **Set your rules in advance,** such as when you'd sell and how much of a drop you'll tolerate. One year is short, and a 20–30% fall in a single stock is common.
- **Mind taxes and fees.** Short-term gains are taxed more heavily in many countries, and frequent trading eats into returns.
- **Consider your situation.** If this is money you'll need soon, or a large share of your savings, a licensed financial adviser is worth consulting. This list isn't personalized advice.

I can also build a more aggressive or more defensive version, or set up a simple checklist for evaluating stocks yourself.
